capabilities.wealth_summary: Commercial Bank of Kuwait (Al-Tijari) is a conventional universal bank whose wealth offer is thin on the evidence found. Its affluent tier is Premier Banking (salary transfer of KD 1,700+ or a term deposit of KD 50,000+) with dedicated officers, lounges, a free World Elite Mastercard and, since 2025, a Premier Family Banking Package. No private banking proposition, funds, managed portfolios, structured products or private-markets offer was found. Investing is delivered through a separate subsidiary, Al-Tijari Financial Brokerage Company (98.16% owned, established 1984), a Boursa Kuwait broker with its own trading app and a CMA portfolio-manager licence for single-client portfolios. A 'Wealth Management Unit' inside Corporate Banking arranges IPO and bond-subscription financing for clients (AR 2025). The CBK mobile app focuses on banking and card services; AR 2025 priorities are funding, self-service digital channels and corporate growth, with no stated wealth strategy. No AUM, client-asset or investor-count figures are published.

segments.name: Premier Banking
segments.eligibility: Salary transfer of KD 1,700 and above, or a term deposit of KD 50,000+ (as published).

private_banking.detail: No separate private banking proposition on the website or in AR 2025; the highest tier found is Premier Banking (S7). A 'Wealth Management Unit' sits within Corporate Banking and arranges IPO and bond financing (AR 2025 p.23).

asset_management.detail: No CBK-branded funds, AUM or asset-management arm found. The brokerage subsidiary holds a CMA licence as portfolio manager for single-client portfolios (S8).

brokerage.detail: Al-Tijari Financial Brokerage Company K.S.C.(Closed): 98.155% owned by CBK per its website (98.16% per AR 2025), established 2 Dec 1984, licensed as qualified securities broker registered at Boursa Kuwait; authorised capital KD 15m, paid-up KD 5.3m. Electronic trading via a desktop client branded 'Accu Trade' and mobile apps (App Store / Google Play); site also links Boursa Kuwait's OTC (unlisted securities) platform. Executes Boursa Kuwait orders; international market access not stated on the pages read.

digital_investing.detail: Brokerage subsidiary's mobile app and web trading (portfolio, orders, notifications, Shariah-compliant share follow section named in the site menu). The CBK Mobile App itself lists banking, cards, KYC and onboarding features; no investing journey found.

advisory.detail: Premier page tells clients to contact Premier Banking Officers 'to discuss your wealth management and banking solutions requirements' (S7) but no advisory service or licence is described for the bank; the brokerage subsidiary's licences cover broker and portfolio manager only.

discretionary.detail: The brokerage subsidiary is licensed to manage portfolios owned by a single client under a written investment policy (S8); no product page, minimum or AUM found.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisory or model-portfolio offer found on the CBK, Premier or brokerage pages opened.

funds_platform.detail: No mutual-fund shelf or fund distribution found.

structured_products.detail: Only treasury 'structured deposits' used for funding and corporate Treasury Sales products (AR 2025) were found; no retail structured products.

private_markets.detail: No private-markets or alternatives offer found.

islamic_wealth.detail: Conventional bank (32% associate Al Cham Islamic Bank, Syria, per AR capital adequacy note). The brokerage site menu includes a 'follow Shariah-compliant shares' section; no Islamic funds or sukuk offer found.

opportunities: Affluent proposition (Premier Banking, KD 1,700 salary / KD 50,000 deposit) is service- and card-led; no investment, fund, advisory or managed-portfolio offer was found on the Premier page (S7) or in AR 2025 (S4).
Investing is limited to Boursa Kuwait trading through a separate brokerage subsidiary and app (S8, S9); the CBK mobile app has no investing journey (S4 pp.29-30).
AR 2025 lists digital onboarding, self-service machines and a Premier Family Banking Package as 2025 launches, indicating appetite for premium and digital packages (S4 pp.20, 29-31).
barriers: Wealth is not a stated strategic priority in AR 2025: management report priorities are funding diversification, self-service digital channels and corporate banking growth (S4).
Leadership in flux: H1 2026 statements are signed by an Acting CEO while the official site still lists the CEO (S3, S1); brokerage subsidiary leadership could not be read.
Brokerage already has its own platform and apps (S8, S9); the parent bank has no stated wealth platform vendor.
Conventional-only bank with a Boursa Kuwait-centric investment base; no Islamic investment offer found (S4, S9).

Mahfouz as CEO), Entrepreneur ME (29 Jul 2026) and Al-Rai (5 Sep 2026, protocol signing with Kuwait Credit Bank) all show Mahfouz as CEO. The 30 Jun 2026 statements dated 28 Jul 2026 are signed by 'Ahmad Khaled Al-Khudhur, Acting CEO', whom the site and AR 2025 list as GM Operations. Kuwait Times (29 Jul 2026) names no CEO. No disclosure, press release or news report about an acting arrangement was found; Boursa Kuwait pages are bot-protected.
discrepancies.resolution: Mahfouz recorded as 'Verified current' because the latest dated sources (29 Jul and 5 Sep 2026) and the official page show her in post; the 28 Jul signature by Al-Khudhur is most consistent with a temporary delegation, but that is not documented. Al-Khudhur recorded as GM Operations with the acting-CEO signature noted. Check Boursa Kuwait disclosures to close.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 lists Ahmad Hamed BoAbbas as Acting GM Corporate Banking; the website lists Kunal Singh as GM International Banking and Acting GM Corporate Banking.
discrepancies.resolution: Website used as more recent; BoAbbas not recorded as current.

open_items: CEO status: Mahfouz is shown as CEO by the official page, the Q1 2026 statements, Entrepreneur ME (29 Jul 2026) and Al-Rai (5 Sep 2026), but the 30 Jun 2026 statements (28 Jul 2026) were signed by Ahmad Al-Khudhur as Acting CEO. No announcement found; the Boursa Kuwait disclosure feed (boursakuwait.com.kw and ifsahdocs.boursakuwait.com.kw answer 403 / 'Request Rejected' to automated reads, checked 2026-10-13) could not be read. Check CBK's disclosures for any Appendix 10 notice of a change or acting arrangement.

Al-Tijari Financial Brokerage Company: executive and board pages read 2026-10-13 (CEO and Deputy CEO - Portfolio Management added; the three other directors of the brokerage not profiled). The brokerage publishes no biographies, so education, career and appointment dates of its two executives are not recorded. Capabilities still rely on its 'About us' page and homepage.
AR 2025 financial statement pages are image-only: notes (fiduciary assets, segment detail, employee numbers) could not be text-searched; fiduciary assets and AUM not located.

Official leadership pages give names and titles only; biographies, education and appointment dates come from AR 2025 (S4, printed pp.47-51 and 67-71). Not profiled (bios in AR 2025): nine directors (Sheikh Talal Mohammad AlSabah, Manaf Al-Muhanna, Mohammad Al-Kandari, Yousef Al-Awadhi, Dhari Al-Mudhaf, Tareq Al Jassim, Fahad Al-Bader, Ahmad Wahedi, Husam Al-Bassam), the Board Secretary and the heads of Corporate Communications, Internal Audit, HR, Legal, General Services, AML/CFT and Complaints. Board term runs 2024-2026 (AR 2025 p.47): check the 2027 AGM outcome.

LinkedIn: role-based searches restricted to linkedin.com (CEO, chief digital officer, retail head, treasury and investment head, brokerage CEO / deputy CEO) on 2026-10-13 returned no profile matching a named executive; no URLs recorded. Company LinkedIn recorded from the official site link (https://www.linkedin.com/company/276269); the vanity URL linkedin.com/company/commercial-bank-of-kuwait appears in search results.
Q3 2026 results not yet published at 12 Oct 2026; add when released.
Premier Banking thresholds are from the website (undated); Network International partnership (Feb 2024) seen in search results only and its go-live status is unknown.
Shareholder table lists only Al Sharq Holding above 5%; ultimate beneficial owner of Al Sharq Holding not researched.

Corporate Banking head: the official page lists Kunal Singh as Acting GM Corporate Banking (with International Banking) while AR 2025 names Ahmad Hamed BoAbbas (Acting GM since Feb 2021); the acting role's date and BoAbbas's current post are not documented. BoAbbas not profiled.
